title: India's first DNA elephant count

scenes.headline: India's first DNA count of wild elephants is out

scenes.label: wild elephants estimated in India
scenes.body: Range 18,255–26,645. Individuals identified from DNA in dung, not by eye.

scenes.headline: The most elephants of any state
scenes.body: In the Western Ghats it is followed by Tamil Nadu (3,136) and Kerala (2,785).

scenes.headline: Don't read it as a crash. Not yet.
scenes.body: Headlines compared it with older counts, but the government says the DNA method sets a new baseline. The next count shows the trend.

caption:
A new number, and a new ruler to measure it.

Elephants have few markings to tell individuals apart, so this survey used DNA mark-recapture, the same logic as camera-trap tiger counts, to estimate how many there are.

Source: Wildlife Institute of India, Status of Elephants in India (SAIEE 2021–25).  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Card + stat news reel on the Oct 2025 elephant estimate whose 'our take' corrects the misleading decline headlines; Karnataka angle for a Bengaluru audience. Elephant videos are Sri Lankan orphanage footage, so wild-context photos used instead.
